description: This plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three measures of Accuracy: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and features a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with rotated tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot contains three lines, all of which include vertical error bars at each data point. The "Final Accuracy" data is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers. It begins at approximately 0.93 at an initial confidence of 0.86, remains relatively steady and high across the x-axis, peaks near 1.00 at an initial confidence of 0.99, and ends at approximately 0.98 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" data is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers. It starts at approximately 0.29 at x=0.86, exhibits a general downward trend to a low of approximately 0.05 at x=0.95, with a notable localized peak of 0.21 at x=0.92, before rising to end at approximately 0.21 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" data is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers. It begins at approximately 0.64 at x=0.86, generally increases to reach peaks of approximately 0.93 at x=0.95 and x=0.99, with a localized dip to 0.77 at x=0.92, and concludes with a sharp decline to approximately 0.77 at x=1.00.
